proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 "⇒" (book/chapter-03.txt lines 113-141). There the integral of f over η_{x,λ}(M) is split into integrals over the blow-ups of disjoint pieces, and the integral over the blow-up of a piece is bounded by sup|f| · H^n(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,λ}(piece)) when f vanishes off B_R(0). This child is Steps 1, 3, 4 and the first half of Step 5 of the parent proof, at one fixed scale r.

Notation: μ := μHE[n]; η := Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.blowUpMap x r, so η(z) = r⁻¹·(z − x); K := closedBall(0, R). For a set S, ∫_S f dμ is the Bochner integral of f with respect to μ restricted to S. Since r > 0, r ≠ 0.

1. (η is injective.) Suppose η(z) = η(w), i.e. r⁻¹·(z − x) = r⁻¹·(w − x). Multiply by r and use r·r⁻¹ = 1 to get z − x = w − x, hence z = w.

2. (Images under η are preimages under a continuous affine map, hence Borel.) Let g(y) := x + r·y. We claim η(T) = g⁻¹(T) for every T ⊆ ℝ^P.
- If y = η(z) with z ∈ T, then g(y) = x + r·(r⁻¹·(z − x)) = x + (z − x) = z ∈ T.
- Conversely, if g(y) ∈ T, then η(g(y)) = r⁻¹·((x + r·y) − x) = r⁻¹·(r·y) = y, so y ∈ η(T).
The map g is continuous, hence Borel measurable, so η(T) = g⁻¹(T) is Borel whenever T is Borel. In particular η(A), η(B) and η(B ∖ A) are Borel; B ∖ A is Borel as a difference of Borel sets.

3. (Integrability on η(T) for Borel T ⊆ B.) Let T be Borel with T ⊆ B.
- η(T) ∩ K ⊆ η(B) ∩ K, so μ(η(T) ∩ K) ≤ μ(η(B) ∩ K) < ∞ by hypothesis.
- f is continuous, hence (a.e.-strongly) measurable, and |f(y)| ≤ C for every y. A measurable function bounded by a constant is integrable on a set of finite measure (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.integrableOn_of_bounded`). So f is integrable on η(T) ∩ K.
- Every y ∈ η(T) ∖ (η(T) ∩ K) lies outside K, so f(y) = 0 by hypothesis. Since η(T) is measurable (Step 2), integrability extends from η(T) ∩ K to η(T) (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`).
We use this with T = A (as A ⊆ B) and with T = B ∖ A.

4. (Splitting.) Because A ⊆ B, B = A ∪ (B ∖ A), hence η(B) = η(A) ∪ η(B ∖ A); the image of a union is the union of the images.
- A and B ∖ A are disjoint and η is injective (Step 1), so η(A) and η(B ∖ A) are disjoint.
- η(B ∖ A) is measurable (Step 2).
- f is integrable on η(A) and on η(B ∖ A) (Step 3).
By additivity of the set integral over a disjoint union (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_union`),
   ∫_{η(B)} f dμ = ∫_{η(A)} f dμ + ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ,
so ∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ.

5. (Localization to K.) Put S := η(B ∖ A) ∩ K. Then S ⊆ η(B ∖ A), η(B ∖ A) is measurable, and f vanishes on η(B ∖ A) ∖ S because those points lie outside K. Hence ∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ = ∫_S f dμ (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero`).

6. (Estimate.) Since B ∖ A ⊆ B, S ⊆ η(B) ∩ K, so μ(S) ≤ μ(η(B) ∩ K) < ∞. Also |f(y)| ≤ C for all y ∈ S. Therefore |∫_S f dμ| ≤ C · μ.real(S), where μ.real(S) = (μ(S)).toReal (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const`, which requires μ(S) < ∞). No sign condition on C or R is used. The cited lemma needs only μ(S) < ∞ and the pointwise bound on S. If R < 0, then K = S = ∅ and both sides are 0.

7. (Conclusion.) Combining Steps 4-6,
   |∫_{η(B)} f dμ − ∫_{η(A)} f dμ| = |∫_{η(B∖A)} f dμ| = |∫_S f dμ| ≤ C · (μ(η(B ∖ A) ∩ closedBall(0, R))).toReal.
This is the asserted inequality; for f : ℝ^P → ℝ the norm ‖·‖ is the absolute value. ∎
key_steps: η = blowUpMap x r is injective (r ≠ 0) and η(T) = (y ↦ x + r·y)⁻¹(T), so η maps Borel sets to Borel sets.
For Borel T ⊆ B, f is integrable on η(T). It is bounded by C on η(T) ∩ closedBall(0,R), a set of measure ≤ μHE[n](η(B) ∩ closedBall(0,R)) < ∞, and it vanishes on the rest of the measurable set η(T).
η(B) is the disjoint union of η(A) and η(B∖A), so setIntegral_union gives ∫_{η(B)} f − ∫_{η(A)} f = ∫_{η(B∖A)} f.
Since f = 0 off closedBall(0,R), ∫_{η(B∖A)} f = ∫_{η(B∖A) ∩ closedBall(0,R)} f. norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const bounds this by C·(μHE[n](η(B∖A) ∩ closedBall(0,R))).toReal.
